theory.intro: The dot product can also be found from lengths and an angle. Multiply the two magnitudes together, then multiply by the cosine of the angle between the vectors.
facts: $\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|\cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the two non-zero vectors.
The result is a scalar, and for two non-zero vectors it has the same sign as $\cos\theta$. A zero vector has no defined direction, and its dot product with any vector is zero.
An acute angle gives a positive dot product, and an obtuse angle gives a negative one.
Perpendicular vectors give $\cos90^{\circ}=0$, so their dot product is zero.
Vectors in the same direction give $\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|$, the largest value possible for these fixed magnitudes.
This formula must agree with the component formula, so the two methods make a useful check on each other.

workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}\\&=|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|\cos135^{\circ}\\&=(9)(2\sqrt{2})\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\\&=-18\end{aligned}$

The tail-to-tail angle is obtuse, so the dot product is negative.

workedExamples.question_text: Two vectors have magnitudes $8$ and $5$. The angle between them is $47^{\circ}$. Find their dot product, correct to two decimal places.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Same direction gives $\theta=0^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\underset{\sim}{p}\cdot\underset{\sim}{q}\\&=(4)(9)\cos0^{\circ}\\&=36\end{aligned}$

(b) Opposite directions gives $\theta=180^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\underset{\sim}{p}\cdot\underset{\sim}{q}\\&=(4)(9)\cos180^{\circ}\\&=-36\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Two non-zero vectors satisfy $\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=-21\sqrt{3}$ and $|\underset{\sim}{b}|=7$. The angle between them is $150^{\circ}$. Find $|\underset{\sim}{a}|$.
Two non-zero vectors satisfy $|\underset{\sim}{u}|=7$, $|\underset{\sim}{v}|=10$ and $\underset{\sim}{u}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v}=-35$. Find the angle between them.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\cos\theta&=\frac{\underset{\sim}{u}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v}}{|\underset{\sim}{u}||\underset{\sim}{v}|}\\\cos\theta&=\frac{-35}{(7)(10)}\\\cos\theta&=-\frac{1}{2}\\\theta&=120^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The angle between vectors lies between $0^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$.
